question: During which of the following dynasties was the Kailasa Temple at Ellora built?
solution: The correct answer is __**Rashtrakutas**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Kailasa Temple** at **Ellora** is one of the largest rock-cut ancient Hindu temples and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. • It was constructed during the reign of the **Rashtrakuta dynasty**, specifically under King **Krishna I**, in the 8th century CE. • This temple is renowned for its architectural brilliance, as it was carved out of a single piece of rock, showcasing the exceptional skill and craftsmanship of that era. • The temple is part of the **Ellora Caves**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and represents a blend of religious harmony as the site includes Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain cave temples. • The Rashtrakutas were known for their patronage of art and architecture, and the Kailasa Temple stands as a testament to their contributions to Indian cultural heritage.
